title: Goodcall: Easy to Build, Priced by the Caller
meta: Honest Goodcall review for 2026: real pricing ($79/mo, billed per unique caller), the genuinely easy drag-and-drop call flow builder, and the real limits (no number porting, no SMS, limited voices).
dek: Goodcall's pitch is simplicity — a drag-and-drop call-flow builder a non-techie can actually use, at $79/mo. The fine print: it's priced per unique caller (not per minute), you can't port your number, and there's no SMS. Here's who that math works for.
verdict_text: Decent if your calls are long or repeat. Goodcall is the easiest of these to set up yourself, and per-unique-caller billing with unlimited minutes is a genuine win when callers talk a while or call back often. But no number porting (you use their number), no SMS, and limited voices are real constraints, and its user rating runs lower than Rosie's. Good for simple, long-call lines; not a full front desk.

blocks.html: Two real strengths. First, the drag-and-drop call-flow builder is usable by a non-technical owner — you can map out “press 1 for a quote” without a developer. Second, pricing is per unique caller with unlimited minutes ($79/mo, ~100 unique callers on Starter), so a long or repeat call doesn't cost extra. For a shop whose calls run long, that model beats per-minute billing.

rows.note: Watch this if your call volume is spiky.
Per-agent pricing gets expensive across locations.
And it does the SMS Goodcall won't.

blocks.label: Fair warning
blocks.claim: “Your 24/7 AI phone agent, set up in minutes.”
blocks.small: Setup really is easy — but: no number porting (you have to use a Goodcall number, so you're changing the number on your truck and website), no SMS (it can't text a lead back), and limited voice options. For a lot of service shops, “can't keep my number and can't text” is a dealbreaker.

workorder.h: We'll set up a line that keeps your number and texts back
workorder.p: Missed-call text-back (yes, actual SMS), fast-response booking, and a human in the loop — on the number already on your truck, so you don't rebuild your whole phone presence around a tool's limits.

ledger_note: The Goodcall link is an affiliate link — we may earn a commission at no cost to you. It never changes the verdict; we flagged the no-porting / no-SMS catches up front.

affiliates.k: Need to keep your number + text back?

faq.a: Starter is about $79/mo for roughly 100 unique callers with unlimited minutes; extra unique callers run ~$0.50–$0.79 each. It's priced per unique caller rather than per minute, which favors long or repeat calls. Multi-location setups get pricier because pricing is also per agent.

Three come up repeatedly: no number porting (you must use a Goodcall number), no SMS (it can't text a lead back), and limited voice options. For many service businesses, not being able to keep your existing number or text customers is a dealbreaker.

Goodcall is easier to build and its per-caller/unlimited-minutes model suits long or repeat calls. Rosie is cheaper to start, has a warmer voice, and gives more minutes per dollar for simple answering. Neither replaces fast human call response for a small shop.
